stages.meaning: Missing CLI commands, undocumented inbox list scope, and observed synthetic unread-to-read changes through direct and MCP readers.

A string ID containing a fragment placed the false query flag in the fragment on the session path; direct Python and registered MCP calls returned read state after the synthetic unread state changed. Token mode preserved state.

Same ten normal groups, same two fragment groups, plus two independent pre-transport admission groups. Each mode challenges 18 invalid Python values and the corresponding MCP inputs; no broker or provider request occurs. A narrow request-admission control preserves positive int/string and leading-zero strings without asserting server semantics for those spellings.

findings: Only the six claimed paths differ from the pinned base.
All API syntax outside the two owned readers is unchanged.
MCP function bodies, signatures and all other metadata remain unchanged.
The CLI matches its original AST after removing exactly six added parser statements and one dispatch branch.
All other runtime source files are byte-identical.
The README retains all existing bytes around one added section.

reviewed_behavior: Explicit false survives real token HTTPX and session-broker envelope encoding for admitted identifiers.
Synthetic unread, read and archived states and complete nested/Unicode JSON are preserved.
Default inbox mapping omits scope; all documented named scopes retain server-side selection.
Opaque continuation queries preserve order and are not rebuilt with first-page filters.
Later-page auth, shape and cycle errors never return partial lists as success.
Actual CLI JSON and registered MCP stdio deliver the expected payloads, errors and unchanged 36-tool inventory.
The fixed shared reader rejects malformed ID spelling/type before transport; descriptions explain positive decimal admission.
limits: Authored loopback contract fixtures; not a real school, Canvas, browser, SSO, cookie or notification receiver.
The session fixture receives the actual broker HTTP envelope and models provider responses; no Playwright execution is claimed.
All remote connections in parent/child receiving are restricted to the fixture port; attachment URLs remain inert metadata.
No owner source, borrowed dependency environment, live profile or shared cache was modified; no dependency downloads.
Valid-ID v1 evidence remains valid for that frozen source, but its original fragment failure is preserved and resolved only by v2.
Root's separate author/inherited test results are not represented as independent replays here.
